info.title: Foundry API v1
info.description:
The JSON API of a Foundry instance, under /api/v1. Every operation except reading this description needs a machine token (the `machineToken` scheme). Every JSON error answer is the `Error` envelope.

An address under /api/v1 that is not one of the operations listed here answers 404 with the uniform not-found envelope, `{"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"not found"}}`, and checks no credential.

The order in which refusals are given:

1. An address under /api/v1 that is not an operation answers 404, with no authentication.
2. On an operation's path, a method the path does not offer answers 405 with an empty body and an `Allow` header, with no authentication. The exception is this description's own path, which answers the 404 envelope.
3. On an operation's path, a missing or bad token answers 401 before any 400, 413, 415 or 422.
4. When revoking a token, 429 can come before 403. No order is promised between them.

get.description: Answers this document, the same bytes for every caller of one release: the copy committed in the repository at crates/foundry-api/openapi.json. It needs no credential and checks none, so a missing, bad or revoked token gets the same answer. HEAD answers the same headers with no body. Any other method answers the uniform 404 envelope.

Cache-Control.description: Always `no-cache`: a client revalidates, so it sees a new release's description.

get.description: Answers every issue of the project. A project with no issues answers an empty array.

parameters.name: project_slug
parameters.description: The project's slug, within the team.

example.title: Sign-in times out behind the proxy

machineToken.description: A machine token: an EdDSA-signed JWT sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A workspace admin mints one, signed in to Foundry, at /admin/tokens; the value is shown once. This API lists and revokes tokens but cannot create one.

Error.description: Every JSON error answer has this shape. `code` is stable and machine-readable; `message` is for people.

ErrorDetail.description: The detail of an error answer.

code.description: A stable, machine-readable code, such as `not_found` or `title_required`.

message.description: A short text for people. It may change between releases.

key.description: The issue's key: the project's key prefix, a hyphen and the number.

number.description: The issue's number within its project.

examples: Sign-in times out behind the proxy

state.description: The lane the issue is in, by its slug. Each project has its own lanes; the defaults are backlog, todo, in_progress, done and cancelled. `in-progress` and `canceled` are accepted as aliases.

Unauthorized.description: Unauthorized. The machine token is missing, malformed, expired, revoked, unknown or not signed by this instance's key; the answer does not say which. Also answered when the token cannot be checked.

NotFound.description: Not found. The same answer, byte for byte, for a team, project, issue or comment that does not exist, one your token cannot reach, and a path that is not part of the API.

MethodNotAllowed.description: Method not allowed. The path exists but does not offer this method. The body is empty, and no credential is checked.

Allow.description: The methods the path offers, such as `GET,HEAD`.

Internal.description: Internal error. Something failed inside the server; the answer carries no detail.

BadPath.description: Bad request. A path segment does not parse: an issue number that is not an integer, or a comment or token id that is not a UUID. The body is plain text from the server framework, not the `Error` envelope, and its wording is not part of the contract.

BadBody.description: Bad request. The body is not valid JSON. The body of this answer is plain text from the server framework, not the `Error` envelope, and its wording is not part of the contract.

PayloadTooLarge.description: Payload too large. The body is larger than 2 MB, and is refused before it is read. The answer is plain text from the server framework, not the `Error` envelope, and its wording is not part of the contract.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: Unsupported media type. The request does not carry `Content-Type: application/json`. The answer is plain text from the server framework, not the `Error` envelope, and its wording is not part of the contract.

UnprocessableBody.description: Unprocessable body. The JSON body lacks a required field or has a field of the wrong type. The answer is plain text from the server framework, not the `Error` envelope, and its wording is not part of the contract.
